ctx.x: And we had Frank Domanian, Eddie Vinson, Vincent, Illinois Jacquet, Jack Kitt, and myself. William Luther Luper was a trombone player, a young boy just come out of Prairie-Prayerview and graduated, and Cootie had come down to catch Milton -- we were under the impression that Milton was, he was the one who told us, that he was gonna take the band and take it to New York, so we had a fire at the Eldorado Ballroom, so we had moved to San Antonio at the Calderman's (UNINTELLIGIBLE) Club there, and Cootie came to San…

out of the band. He picked Eddie Vinson Vincent, he picked William Luver Luther, he picked me. Out of the three, I was the only one who refused, so Eddie went, with Cootie Williams. Luver Luther left to go and got on the bus and got to St. Louis, and I don't know what happened; he took sick and died in the hospital. He never got to New York .... trombone player, terrific, never got there. I don't know; it was like tomatoe poisoning, or something like that.

And incidentally, this Monday we had Ellington [Field] playing here, and I'm carrying him on my book of insurance, and I had to strike him because after four weeks, you lapsed him, and I counted four weeks out of my pocket and (unintelligible) man, I can't afford it.
